scenario: Rectangular barge, sharp bilge (no measurable bilge radius), no bilge keels, zero speed, B/T 3 to 8, roll axis near the waterline
primary_method: Sharp-cornered barge eddy formula (Ikeda, Fujiwara and Katayama 1993; Chakrabarti 2001 eq. 35) plus friction, added to the solver's radiation damping; amplitude iterated with the RAO
cross_check: Journee and Massie (2001) eq. 7.174 decay fit (total, G at the waterline); Gu and Day (2015) B/T 6 decay
screening_damping_pct: Total about 6 to 13 % of critical at 5 to 10 deg for B/T 4 to 6, rising to about 18 % at 15 deg (Journee fit, G at the waterline); eq. 35 viscous part is proportional to amplitude (about 1.9 % per deg on the generic barge) and is iterated, not capped
basis: Gu and Day (2015) 10.6 % total from a 15 deg release, B/T 6; Journee and Massie eq. 7.174: 9.0 %, 13.4 % and 17.8 % at 5, 10 and 15 deg for B/T 6; eq. 35 at the 15 deg release amplitude is 35 % above Gu and Day
avoid: Sectional Ikeda C_R formula: its f3 term switches off near sigma 0.999 and it underestimates sharp barges

scenario: Barge or box with a clearly rounded bilge (tested at R/T 0.31, R/B 0.10), no bilge keels
primary_method: Sectional Ikeda eddy coefficient C_R with the actual bilge radius, integrated over stations
cross_check: Kim, Kim and Ha (2015) box decay: 1.0 to 1.3 % total at 5 to 15 deg (R/B 0.10)
screening_damping_pct: Total 1 to 2 % of critical at 5 to 15 deg
basis: Sectional formula 0.4 to 1.2 % against Kim et al. 1.0 to 1.3 % total; eq. 35 is 6 to 14 times the measurement
avoid: Eq. 35: it has no bilge-radius term and overestimates by up to an order of magnitude

scenario: Barge with a small bilge radius, between a sharp corner and the tested rounded bilge (no test evidence in this range)
primary_method: Bracket with both eq. 35 and the sectional formula; for motion response use the lower value until a test or 2-D CFD decides
digitalmodel_route: barge_roll_damping and eddy_damping_sections side by side
cross_check: 2-D URANS forced roll of the midship section
screening_damping_pct: Between the two formulas; they differ by a factor of 1.6 to 13 on the generic barge
basis: Generic barge at 10 deg: sectional 11.6 % at R/T 0.01 and 1.5 % at R/T 0.3 against eq. 35 19.1 % (calculation, not a test)
avoid: A single formula without stating the radius

scenario: Barge with bilge keels or skegs at the bilge
primary_method: Eddy part by the bilge shape (above) plus the Ikeda bilge-keel normal-force and hull-pressure terms (Chakrabarti 2001 eqs. 46-60); ITTC 2024 KC-number C_D fit where KC is 0.3 to 20
cross_check: Kim et al. (2015) K1 to K3 decay; Kjaer et al. (2024) keel raised the quadratic coefficient 3.7 to 5.7 times
screening_damping_pct: Total 3 to 15 % of critical at 5 to 15 deg for small to large keels
basis: Kim et al. (2015) 2.6 to 14.9 % total; generic barge with a 0.3 m keel over half the length: +57 %
avoid: Ikeda keel-hull interaction term at large amplitude or large keels (Bassler and Reed 2009); keels near the free surface at shallow draught

scenario: Wide shallow barge-like hull with B/T above about 8 or a high KG (installation vessel, crane barge with deck load, jack-up afloat)
primary_method: Model decay test or CFD (2-D URANS forced roll; 3-D decay at full-scale Reynolds number); empirical formulas only as an upper bound
digitalmodel_route: barge_roll_damping as an upper bound only
cross_check: Kjaer et al. (2024) B/T 8.2: about 5.3 % total at model scale, lower at high KG, 62 to 90 % lower at full scale
screening_damping_pct: Below 5 % total until a test or CFD justifies more
basis: Kjaer et al. (2024): ITTC 2011 barge model significantly overestimated; Haver (2016, abstract): barge model inappropriate at B/T 10
avoid: Eq. 35 or Journee and Massie as design values; model-scale damping without a scale check

scenario: Ship-shaped hull within B/d 2.5 to 4.5, C_B 0.5 to 0.85, C_M 0.90 to 0.99, with or without bilge keels
primary_method: Full Ikeda component method (ITTC 7.5-02-07-04.5, 2024) by stations, with the bilge-keel terms
cross_check: Simplified Ikeda regression (Kawahara, Maekawa and Ikeda 2009) inside its stated range; model decay test
screening_damping_pct: 2 to 5 % of critical viscous at 10 deg with keels (illustrative ship 2.2 %); model decays 5 to 15 % total (Smith 2019)
basis: ITTC 7.5-02-07-04.5 (2011, 2021, 2024); illustrative container-like ship 2.21 % viscous at 10 deg
avoid: Simplified Ikeda outside its regression range (for example barges with C_B above 0.85)

scenario: FPSO, FSO or barge-type floater with bilge keels, zero speed, long service
primary_method: Ikeda components for screening; model decay test or 2-D URANS forced roll of the midship section with keels for design
cross_check: Koop et al. (2019, abstract): 2-D CFD within 2 % of the 2-D test
screening_damping_pct: 10 % of critical viscous when no data (ABS DLA Sec. 4/5.7); replace with test or CFD for design
basis: ABS DLA FPSO Guide p. 19; ABS DLA Vessels Guide p. 26
avoid: A default value carried into detailed design

scenario: Any hull with forward speed or in current
primary_method: Zero-speed components with the Ikeda speed factors: eddy eq. 36, lift eqs. 37-38, friction eq. 12, wave eqs. 39-43
cross_check: None for barges in current: the paper's suggestion has no test basis
screening_damping_pct: Lower than zero speed for the eddy part (eq. 36 halves it where 0.04 omega L/U = 1); use the zero-speed value with a stated basis
basis: Chakrabarti (2001) eqs. 12, 36-43; Fig. 6 barge total falls from about 16.5 % to 6 % by Fn 0.1
avoid: Applying speed factors to slow drift or current without a test

scenario: Roll amplitude above about 15 to 20 deg, especially with bilge keels
primary_method: Large-amplitude bilge-keel model (Bassler and Reed 2009; ITTC from 2011) or URANS
cross_check: Yildiz et al. (2016): Ikeda agrees with URANS to 20 deg and overestimates beyond
screening_damping_pct: No screening value; the formulas are outside their evidence above 15 deg
basis: Chakrabarti (2001) p. 924: formulas reliable to about 5 deg; examples at 10 deg
avoid: Linear extrapolation of eq. 35 beyond 15 deg

scenario: Column-stabilised unit or other non-ship hull
primary_method: Morison drag on columns and pontoons in a time-domain model, or forced-oscillation CFD
basis: OC6 Phase Ia, NREL report 80803 (search summary only)

scenario: Frequency-domain RAO in irregular seas (any hull)
primary_method: Equivalent linear damping by stochastic linearisation: replace (8/3pi) omega phi_a by sqrt(8/pi) times the roll-velocity standard deviation; iterate with the response
digitalmodel_route: equivalent_linear_damping for harmonic roll; stochastic form by the caller
cross_check: Time-domain simulation with the quadratic term
screening_damping_pct: Iterated value at the design sea state
basis: DNV-RP-C206 Sec. 6.6 (iterate on roll angle); Kjaer et al. (2024) p. 9 on entering quadratic terms
avoid: A single harmonic amplitude for an irregular sea

scenario: Any hull at concept stage with no hull lines, mass data or tests
primary_method: ABS default as the viscous part, then the scenario row above as soon as B/T, bilge shape and KG are known
screening_damping_pct: 10 % of critical viscous (ABS); flag any value above 10 % and recommend a model test if resonance falls in the operating range
avoid: Quoting the default as a finding

scenario: Transportation barge in a time-domain or nonlinear frequency-domain motion run (AQWA)
primary_method: Bilge vortex-shedding quadratic damping (Robinson and Stoddart 1986), as built into the AQWA nonlinear roll damping option, with the bilge radius as input
digitalmodel_route: Not this module; use eq. 35 or the sectional formula as the independent check
cross_check: Eq. 35 (sharp bilge) or sectional Ikeda (rounded bilge) at the simulated amplitude
screening_damping_pct: Report the equivalent % of critical at the simulated amplitude and compare with the barge rows above
basis: AQWA documentation, Nonlinear Roll Damping (Robinson and Stoddart 1986; bilge keel per ITTC 7.5-02-07-04.5, 2011)
avoid: A solver option used without stating its bilge radius and shedding criterion
